# Celebrating Microsoft Ignite with Azure region expansion in Toronto


Elastic Cloud Serverless coverage rises to 13 Azure regions worldwide


By


[Lucy Wang](https://www.elastic.co/blog/author/lucy-wang)[Brian Bergholm](https://www.elastic.co/blog/author/brian-bergholm)

###### Summary


- Elastic Cloud Serverless is built on a cloud-native stateless architecture that uses Azure Blob Storage to manage and search petabytes of data.


- Handle massive data volumes and complex queries with dynamic auto-scale that adjusts in real time to changes in demand, minimizes latency, and ensures the fastest response.


- Elastic Cloud Serverless has expanded to another region in Canada to support customers with total coverage of 35 regions globally across hyperscalers.


We’re pleased to announce the availability of


[Elastic Cloud Serverless](https://www.elastic.co/cloud/serverless) on Microsoft Azure in the Toronto (canadacentral) region starting November 18, 2026. This expansion brings our Azure coverage to 13 regions and our total coverage to


[35 regions around the globe](https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/deploy/elastic-cloud/regions) .


## Elastic Cloud Serverless: The fastest way to start and scale search, observability, and security on Elastic


Elastic Cloud Serverless handles sizing, sharding, scaling, and upgrades, so your team can ship apps that retrieve answers accurately, fix outages before customers notice, and stop threats before they become breaches. Storage is decoupled from compute and indexing from search, so queries stay fast and relevant as data grows to petabytes. Create a project in minutes with the latest AI capabilities built in, from Jina models, Context Engine, and Elastic Agent Builder to Elastic® nightshift AI SRE. Pay only for what you use.


-


**Deploy in minutes, query across petabytes.**


Spin up a serverless project in minutes and let it scale automatically as workloads grow to petabytes, with no infrastructure to manage along the way.


-


**Deliver AI faster on one platform.**


Build AI apps, investigate incidents, and hunt threats on a single platform for every data type: documents, vectors, logs, traces, and metrics. Every answer draws on precise, grounded context from the platform more than 18,000 organizations and 75% of the Fortune 100 already run on.


-


**Skip the infrastructure.**


No clusters to size, no shards to balance, no version upgrades to schedule. Elastic runs it, backed by a 99.95% monthly uptime SLA on Platinum and Enterprise.


-


**Pay for efficient usage.**


Serverless bills on what you ingest, search, and retain. Data lives in low-cost object storage and stays fully searchable, and because storage is decoupled from compute, you pay less per unit of usage. Pay as you go monthly or prepay with ECUs, which work across Elastic Cloud Hosted and Serverless.


## Serverless capabilities


-


**Cross-project search (GA):**


Teams can now


query across multiple serverless projects without moving or duplicating data. Security analysts, SREs, and app engineers get a unified search experience across regions, cloud providers, and project types, without the operational overhead of centralizing data.


-


**Audit logs for Serverless (GA):**


Elastic Cloud Serverless now delivers audit logs straight into your Security or Observability Serverless project. They are encrypted in transit and at rest and are ready for compliance. Route only the logs that matter in your organization, across regions and cloud providers. Drop unneeded events before delivery, so you do not pay to ingest noise, while cost stays proportional to data volume and retention. Simply choose your source and destination projects, retention, and the events to filter, and Elastic handles everything else.


-


**Decoupled architecture:**


The indexing tier is separate from the search tier. This allows workloads to scale independently and reliably using hardware optimized for each specific use case.


-


**Low latency on storage object:**


Data is stored in cloud object storage (Azure Blob Storage) using thin indexing shards. An intelligent caching layer sits on top to deliver low-latency query parallelization.


-


**Zero management and auto-scaling:**


Elastic handles infrastructure sizing, shard balancing, data backups, and business continuity. It scales resources dynamically in real time to handle high-demand ingestion or peak querying seamlessly. Projects are versionless. Elastic deploys automatic security patches, upgrades, and feature updates in the background without affecting API configurations or client compatibility.


## Serverless use cases


### Ecommerce and catalog search


Retailers frequently experience massive, unpredictable traffic spikes during events like flash sales, forcing them to over-provision infrastructure and pay for unused compute during idle periods just to avoid downtime or poor customer experience. With Serverless, the decoupled architecture automatically scales compute up during traffic surges (or prescale search tier ahead with Search Min VCUs) and scales it down when traffic normalizes. Customers only pay for the exact compute used, ensuring high-performance catalog retrieval.


### MSSPs and global enterprises running a Center of Excellence


Their data lives in many regions and across cloud providers. With cross-project search on Elastic Cloud Serverless, teams query all of their linked serverless projects from one place, as if the data were local, with no data movement and no rearchitecture required.


### Application observability and log analytics


During a system outage, applications can generate a massive spike in error logs. In a coupled architecture, this sudden ingest spike may consume all cluster resources, causing the actual search queries used to find the root cause to slow down. Serverless independently separates indexing compute from search compute, meaning a massive spike in log ingestion will dynamically scale the indexing tier without any scale up for the search tier. This allows SREs to query their observability data in real time during a critical incident.


### Security analytics and threat hunting


SOC teams can hit the ground running all on an open and extensive platform. Search across all security data in one place with ES|QL, Timeline, and prebuilt anomaly detection jobs for host and network behavior. Elastic AI Agent generates and explains ES|QL queries from natural language, and Agent Builder lets teams build hunting agents grounded in their own data. Hunters follow leads across logs, endpoints, and cloud proactively.


## Serverless project types


Elastic provides four serverless project types on Elastic Cloud. Follow these guides to get started with your serverless project:


-


[Elasticsearch Serverless](https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/search/get-started) **:**


Build powerful, scalable search and analytics applications across structured data, logs, metrics, documents, and vectors as part of a broader Elastic Stack.


-


[Elasticsearch Vector Database](https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/vector-database/get-started) **:**


Build embedding-driven workloads such as semantic search, RAG, and AI-powered retrieval. Built-in models and vector-optimized defaults mean less configuration and faster time to production.


-


[Elastic Observability Serverless](https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/observability/get-started) **:**


Monitor your own platforms and services using powerful machine learning and analytics tools with your logs, metrics, traces, and APM data.


-


[Elastic Security Serverless](https://www.elastic.co/docs/solutions/security/get-started#create-sec-serverless-project) **:**


Detect, investigate, and respond to threats with SIEM, endpoint protection, and AI-powered analytics capabilities.


## Getting started with Elastic Cloud Serverless on Azure


To try Elastic Cloud Serverless on Azure, visit


[Microsoft Marketplace](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/elastic.ec-azure-pp?ocid=cloud-serverless-recap2025) and follow the steps below. You can either start a seven-day free trial or employ any of your existing credits. Your Elastic subscription will appear in your Microsoft Azure consolidated billing, and your spend counts toward your Azure cloud commitment. Or, you can


[sign up](https://cloud.elastic.co/serverless-registration) or


[log in](https://cloud.elastic.co/) to the Elastic Cloud console and follow the steps below. Either way, you can easily monitor and analyze your Elastic usage and costs right from the Elastic Cloud console.


1.


Create a


**Serverless project**


.


2.


For


**Elasticsearch**


,


**Elastic Observability**


,


**Elastic Security**


, or


**Elasticsearch Vector Database**


projects, select


**Azure**


as the cloud provider and then choose your preferred Azure region.


3. Click


**Create project**


, and your Elastic Cloud Serverless project will be provisioned.


If you have any questions or want to learn more, visit our


[documentation](https://www.elastic.co/docs/current/serverless) .


For more information, check out our


[roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/elastic/projects/2066/views/2?filterQuery=&sliceBy%5Bvalue%5D=Serverless) or read why


[Vectorize.io](https://www.elastic.co/customers/vectorize-io) and


[Docusign](https://www.elastic.co/customers/docusign) chose Elastic Cloud Serverless.
